clue.text: I snarl — hag disrupting a blissful situation

indicators.note: the hag is said to be disrupting the words before it, so the letters of all three words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone snarls at a crone who has barged in and spoiled a perfectly happy moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupting' tells you to rearrange the nine letters of I, SNARL and HAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La is the hidden paradise of James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon, so the name stands for any idyllic state of bliss.

clue.text: Keen to get a collection of efficient knives?

explanation.surface: A cook is keen to get hold of a good set of knives.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer literally: a set of blades that are well honed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp-set is an old term for eager or hungry; read as two words it also describes a well-honed set of kitchen blades.

clue.text: Officer laid into a bounder with energy — there's public praise

indicators.note: the officer is laid into the words that follow, so his letters go inside them

parts.note: a bounder is an old word for a cad, a dishonourable man
Col is the abbreviation for Colonel, a military officer
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An officer lays into a scoundrel, and with some vigour, earning public applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid into' looks like a beating, but it is the container signal; 'bounder' is an old-fashioned British word for a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of acclaim given openly.

clue.text: 'Not much good getting mature' daughter moaned

indicators.note: only a small part of the word good is wanted, its opening letter

parts.note: mature fruit is ripe
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A daughter grumbles that getting older is not much fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words look like what she said, but they are pure wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Griped is a colloquial word for complained, grumbled.

clue.text: Killer shows nice manners bumping some characters off

indicators.note: knocking off letters from both ends of nice manners leaves a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A murderer is surprisingly polite while bumping people off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumping off' suggests murder, chiming with 'Killer', but it means dropping letters: take N off the front and NERS off the back of 'nice manners'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceman is slang for a cold-blooded professional assassin.

clue.text: Wild boar is ma cooking? Fantastic grub!

indicators.note: cooking the words before it means putting their letters through a change, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A wild boar being roasted by mum: what a splendid meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' only belongs to the surface picture of a wild boar; 'cooking' is the instruction to shuffle BOAR IS MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, hence any exceptionally delicious dish.

clue.text: Distinguishing feature of bird artist captured

indicators.note: the bird has captured the artist, holding his letters inside its own

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A painter catches the characteristic look of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a characteristic quality marking out one person or thing.

clue.text: Pretty bird, one very short, took food

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
I is the Roman numeral for one
V is the short form of very
to take food is to eat, past tense ate

explanation.surface: A lovely little bird, one that is very small, has had a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adjective describing the bird but is a verb meaning to smarten.
explanation.definitionFit: To titivate is to make small improvements to one's appearance, to spruce up.

clue.text: A woman beginning to knit jacket

parts.note: Nora is a woman's name

indicators.note: only the start of the word knit is used, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A woman is starting to knit herself a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a weatherproof hooded coat.

clue.text: Spring festival has movable time — a problem

indicators.note: the time letter is described as movable, so it shifts to a new place in the festival's name

parts.note: Easter is the Christian festival held in spring

explanation.surface: A spring festival whose date shifts each year poses a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Easter really is a movable feast, which is the clever surface; here 'movable' sends the T of EASTER to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a tricky puzzle or brain-teaser.

clue.text: Record for being roguish I have

parts.note: arch means mischievous, slyly playful
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A rascal boasts of a record for mischievous behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a collection of historical documents or stored records.

clue.text: Tot knocked back before one has endless marijuana — some festival!

indicators.note: the turned drink comes before the remaining pieces
drinks are knocked back, and here the word for a tot is turned backwards

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits, a dram
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word for marijuana loses its final letter

parts.note: grass is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink and then has a joint: quite a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking but turns DRAM into MARD; 'endless' cuts GRASS to GRAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras is the carnival held on Shrove Tuesday, famously in New Orleans and Rio.

clue.text: Not completely understanding who will take over in emergency

definitions.text: who will take over in emergency

indicators.note: only part of the word understanding is wanted, a stretch running inside it

explanation.surface: Someone lacking full comprehension is asked who would take charge in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop UNDER from the front and G from the end of 'understanding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a substitute who replaces someone absent.

clue.text: One delivering corporal punishment or kiss?

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone dishing out a slap might instead be giving a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A smacker is literally one who spanks or slaps, and colloquially a loud, hearty kiss.

clue.text: It's desperate special offer at the takeaway?

explanation.surface: A fish-and-chip shop slashes its prices in a desperate bid for trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading imagines a chip shop cutting its chip prices.
explanation.definitionFit: 'When the chips are down' is an idiom for a moment of crisis; literally, fried potatoes reduced in price.

clue.text: Symbol with lines carried by Noah's boy on his boat

indicators.note: the lines are carried inside the name of Noah's son

parts.note: Ham was one of Noah's three sons in Genesis
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for lines
Noah's vessel was the ark

explanation.surface: Noah's son carries a sign marked with lines aboard the ark.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed below, so ARK follows the HALLM part.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallmark is an official stamp on precious metal, and so any distinguishing mark or emblem.

clue.text: Cheese leaves nasty smear in vessel

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go in the vessel, between its letters

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel

indicators.note: a nasty smear is a distorted one, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Cheese has left an unpleasant stain inside a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb of departure but is only a link; 'nasty' shuffles the smear before it goes 'in' the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese from the Parma region.

clue.text: Light work that's tricky to repeat

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward or twisted, so the letters of to repeat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of music that is difficult to perform again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' tells you to rearrange the eight letters of TO REPEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short, light-hearted opera with spoken dialogue.

clue.text: Don't ignore refusal to get beaten badly

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: badly beaten means knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is warned not to ignore a refusal or face a bad beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't ignore' is a fair verbal definition: the Latin phrase is an instruction to take notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nota bene is Latin for 'note well', a written instruction to pay attention to something.

clue.text: Rodent-killer's left to catch snake

indicators.note: the rodent-killer is about to catch the letter for left, holding it within

parts.note: a ratter is a dog or cat good at killing rats

explanation.surface: A dog that kills rats has been left to catch a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Rodent-killer's' is just 'is', a link; 'to catch' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is the informal name for a rattlesnake.

clue.text: King is seizing revolutionary's loot

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: the word is takes hold of the revolutionary, enclosing his name

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A king is grabbing hold of a rebel's plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Riches are wealth or treasure, such as booty taken by force.

clue.text: Golfer will walk this way? Exactly!

explanation.surface: Someone says a golfer will walk precisely this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading treats the phrase literally: a golfer walks toward a tee to play.
explanation.definitionFit: 'To a T' means perfectly or precisely; a golfer heads to the tee to begin each hole.

clue.text: East Anglian town needs hospital department? Protest

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, in eastern England
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A small Norfolk town campaigns for a hospital department of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: DISS is a small town in Norfolk, part of East Anglia in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement or objection to official views.

clue.text: Remove weapon from mad sir on the rampage

indicators.note: a rampage is wild, uncontrolled action, so the letters of mad sir run riot

explanation.surface: A crazed gentleman goes on a violent spree and must be disarmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rampage' rearranges MAD SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm is to take away someone's weapons.

clue.text: Make a mistake getting schoolchildren upset

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is upset, turned upside down so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: schoolchildren are pupils

explanation.surface: A teacher blunders and upsets the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' in a down clue means turn the word upside down, so PUPILS is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip up is to err or blunder.

clue.text: Cold and safe, lacking appeal

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
harmless means safe, posing no danger

explanation.surface: Something cold and safe is dull and unattractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmless means without charm, unattractive.

clue.text: One has to manage without all the members alas

definitions.text: One has to manage without all the members alas

parts.words: One has to manage without all the members alas
parts.note: reads like a club short of people, but members are limbs, and this person lives without some of them

explanation.surface: A sad club secretary must cope after the membership has dwindled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' is an old word for limbs, the key to the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has had a limb removed must live without all their bodily limbs.

clue.text: Meat that sounds like something risky

indicators.note: the clue states plainly that the answer is pronounced like a word for a risky thing

parts.note: a stake is money put at risk in a bet

explanation.surface: A cut of meat whose name sounds like a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak is a thick slice of beef or other meat for grilling.

clue.text: Enamel apt to be unreliable for identification sign

indicators.note: letters that are unreliable will not stay in place, so enamel apt is rearranged

explanation.surface: Enamel is likely to be a poor material for a sign on a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be unreliable' rearranges ENAMEL APT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nameplate is a plaque on a door or desk showing the occupant's name.
